query: Starting from crystalline, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles composed of five or more metals, what single intervention could overcome the unresolved risk of structural or chemical instability during operation in the 773–1173 K catalytic regime? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, the mechanism by which it would preserve stability, the predicted outcome relative to the same nanoparticles without the intervention, relevant temperature, time, and compositional boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a thermal-exposure experiment with measurements and failure criteria that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a minor amount of a refractory metal, such as tungsten or molybdenum, into the near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles can overcome the risk of structural or chemical instability during operation in the 773–1173 K catalytic regime.
generation.material_initial_state: Crystalline, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles composed of five or more metals
generation.intervention: Introduction of a minor amount of a refractory metal, such as tungsten or molybdenum
generation.conditions: Operation in the 773–1173 K catalytic regime for hours to days
generation.mechanism: The refractory metal atoms can act as stabilizers, reducing the diffusion rates and suppressing the formation of defects, thereby preserving the structural and chemical stability of the nanoparticles
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved stability and catalytic performance of the nanoparticles compared to those without the intervention
generation.baseline: Nanoparticles without the introduction of a refractory metal
generation.boundary: Temperature range of 773–1173 K, time range of hours to days, and compositional range of near-equiatomic solid-solution
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount and type of refractory metal to be introduced, as well as the potential effects on the catalytic activity and selectivity

falsification_experiment.design: Thermal-exposure experiment with in-situ characterization techniques, such as X-ray diffraction, transmission electron microscopy, and energy-dispersive spectroscopy
measurements: Structural and chemical changes, catalytic activity and selectivity
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the nanoparticles with the introduced refractory metal exhibit significant structural or chemical instability, or if their catalytic performance is not improved compared to those without the intervention, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) have excellent mechanical properties, which could make them the substitutes of some superalloys. However, the high melting point of refractory HEAs leads to processing problems when using traditional processing techniques. In this study, a single BCC solid solution of NbMoTaW alloy was formed by selective laser melting (SLM) with a linear energy density of up to 2.83 J/mm. The composition distribution was analyzed, and the element with a lower melting point and lower density showed a negative deviation (no more than 5%) of the molar ratio in the formed alloy. The HEA shows an excellent microstructure, microhardness, and corrosion resistance performance compared with traditional superalloys, making it a new substitute metal with great application prospects in aerospace and energy fields.

Abstract A novel metal matrix composite based on the NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy (HEA) was designed by the in-situ formation method. The microstructure, phase evolution, and compression mechanical properties at room temperature of the composite are investigated in detail. The results confirmed that the composite was primarily composed of body-centered cubic solid solution with a small amount of titanium carbides and alumina. With the presence of approximately 7.0 vol. % Al 2 O 3 and 32.2 vol. % TiC reinforced particles, the compressive fracture strength of the composite (1542 MPa) was increased by approximately 50% compared with that of the as-cast NbMoCrTiAl HEA. In consideration of the superior oxidation resistance, the P/M NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy composite could be considered as a promising high temperature structural material. Keywords: high entropy alloys, metal matrix composites, mechanical properties

High entropy or multi principal element alloys are a promising and relatively young concept for designing alloys. The idea of creating alloys without a single main alloying element opens up a wide space for possible new alloy compositions. High entropy alloys based on refractory metals such as W, Mo, Ta or Nb are of interest for future high temperature applications e.g., in the aerospace or chemical industry. However, producing refractory metal high entropy alloys by conventional metallurgical methods remains challenging. For this reason, the feasibility of laser-based additive manufacturing of the refractory metal high entropy alloy W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 by laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB/M) is investigated in the present work. In-situ alloy formation from mixtures of easily available elemental powders is employed to avoid an expensive atomization of pre-alloyed powder. It is shown that PBF-LB/M of W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 is in general possible and that a complete fusion of the powder mixture without a significant number of undissolved particles is achievable by in-situ alloy formation during PBF-LB/M when selecting favorable process parameter combinations.
